dedupe_keys.name: nyu v lab srisk systemic risk measures

description: SRISK is a measure of systemic risk that the cited literature describes as a conditional capital shortfall of financial firms. The V-Lab of NYU Stern publishes SRISK estimates on its website: a global summary of systemic risk by country in billions of US dollars, relative to GDP, and tables of the firms that contribute most, with SRISK in millions of dollars, long-run marginal expected shortfall (LRMES) and leverage (LVG), for global and U.S. financial firms. The method is documented in the related papers listed on the page, including Brownlees and Engle (2016) on SRISK as a conditional capital shortfall measure and Acharya, Engle and Richardson (2012) on capital shortfall. Coverage is global, by country and for global and U.S. financial firms. Access to the tables and charts on the site is free; download terms and licence are not stated on the page read. Caveats: estimates rely on equity market data and model assumptions, and the page does not state which firms are covered. For simulation it provides firm- and country-level indicators of financial fragility for systemic risk and contagion scenarios in the financial sector. Related catalogue records include the OFR Bank Systemic Risk Monitor and the OFR Financial Stress Index.
